reviewer.name: Claude Sonnet, fresh subagent (preservation reviewer)
reviewer.origin: Claude Agent tool subagent, model sonnet, a fresh context with only this brief and its files, launched 2026-10-26 by session_01Mxpoi6tFT3FgKmBvtGjRtS (the writer's session)

evidence: Judged: “If you can’t do this in a loving way today, just put your hands there and see what you feel, no faking required.” I read DRAFT, SOURCE and CONTEXT (the draft appears once, as the last sentence of the Inner child love paragraph) and compared word by word. PRESERVATION. Against the words it replaces (“If you can’t do this in a loving way today, just put your hands there and see what you feel. You don’t have to fake it!”) the first clause is identical; the whole delta is “. You don’t have to fake it!” becoming “, no faking required.” That is the same permission at the same strength (the exclamation mark and the second sentence go); nothing is added (no claim, condition, person or number) and nothing of the fallback is lost. Against his inner child guide’s line (“No warmth today? Then rest your hands there and notice what you find, no faking required.”) every part maps both ways: today and no warmth, hands there, noticing, and the release, which is his three words verbatim in the same place and attached to the same noticing. The small differences (put for rest, just, see what you feel for notice what you find) are already in the words being replaced, not made by this change; feel is a touch narrower than find but still lets the reader find nothing, so who does what and how much is asked are unchanged. It also agrees with his published point (do not recite the words like an incantation you hope the subconscious will grade; say them the way you would to a frightened child you actually love): it is a permission, which “Don’t fake it.” was not, and the sentence before it still asks that the reader actually talk to the inner child. It does what the_change says: one sentence, ending on his own words from the guide. I cannot check from these files that the first clause is batch 479’s sample ch word for word. Typography is clean: curly apostrophe as in the context, no space before the full stop, no its/it’s slip, no quote marks added. CONTEXT: reads right; “this” is the practice just given, said in a loving way (a deliberate callback to “say to yourself in a loving way”, not unearned repetition), and “there” is the heart and solar plexus named before. Sentences outside the change (for example “Here is some inner child love.”) were read only for how they bear on the draft. TELLS: I answered T01 to T29 and C01 to C04 on the draft in its context and found none actually happening, so resolved_tell_ids is empty. The nearest calls: T10, it is a permission but not the “you don’t have to X before Y” packaging, it is his own published phrase, and it answers the demand in the sentence before it (the old “You don’t have to fake it!” also repeated the “You don’t have to” frame of the quoted line “You don’t have to fix it”, which is now gone); T22, it reassures and instructs but from a reason of his own and at the same density as his own line; T20 and T28, it does end the paragraph and, by CONTEXT.txt, the section (so the ADMISSION.json line that it “is not the end of its section” is wrong for this context), but it closes on a practical step with his idiom as a clause tail, not a standalone polished line, and adds no lesson, summary or uplift; T29, the fallback is a new step and the paragraph is incomplete without it; T02, the sequence is the practice itself and the change turns two sentences into one. LINTER: “D9 follows the source order” accepted: a one-sentence swap of a one-point fallback has no outline to mirror, the order is his line’s, and the T13 and T09 checks it points to are clear (the paragraph keeps its aside “who is scared to death”, the sentence notices that faking is what the demand before it invites, and only the last sentence of the paragraph is the change). “E36/E41 heavy second person” accepted: 13.0 is three second-person words (you, your, you) in a 23-word sentence, about the density of his own line (2 in 16 words), inside a paragraph that speaks to the reader throughout as a guided practice; it is not scenery or a run of coaching lines. Nothing unresolved.
